title: Preflight capture template for flaky GPU reset chains
summary: A pragmatic preflight checklist and structured capture template to use during on-call for intermittent GPU reset chains (soft resets, driver restarts, nvlink negotiation failures). Focuses on minimal reproducible capture steps, prioritized fields to collect, and quick heuristics to decide next actions.
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, pragmatic capture template for on-call SREs to run when encountering intermittent GPU reset chains (the class of symptoms that looks like: repeated soft ECC spikes -> short nvlink renegotiation -> driver panic -> kernel oops -> node reboot). The goal is to collect a compact, high-signal bundle so engineers can triage without long back-and-forth. Use this as a preflight when the node is still up, or immediately after a soft-reset event but before large-scale cleanup.

When to use:
- Node observed returning transient errors (correctable ECC bursts) followed by short driver hangs or a single kernel panic in the last 24h.
- Noise in telemetry: increased reset_count for a GPU, nvlink error counters incrementing, or node-level reboot waves.
- Early on-call suspicion of link/firmware timing issues rather than clear hardware failure.

Quick rules of engagement:
1) If node is actively degraded (training/serve impacted), run the FAST CAPTURE only, then failover traffic.
2) If node still healthy, run FULL CAPTURE; avoid reboots unless safe.
3) Tag capture artifacts with incident id and exact epoch time (UTC).
4) Preserve driver/firmware versions and kernel image names in every artifact file name.

FAST CAPTURE (3–5 min) - minimum that must be attached to incident:
- /var/log/messages (last 1h) or journalctl -u kmod-driver -S "-1 hour" --no-pager
- dmesg | tail -n 200 (capture kernel ring since suspect time)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,enc-util --format=csv -lms 1000 (3 samples) OR equivalent vendor tool
- nvlink status: python /usr/local/bin/nvlink-check.py --brief (or nvidia-smi nvlink --display=all)
- ipmitool sel elist recent (BMC events around the same time)
- lspci -vvv -s <gpu-pci-id> (single snapshot)
- top -b -n1 | head -n50 (process snapshot)
- small notes.txt: who ran capture, node name, time UTC, incident id, reproducer commands used (if any)

FULL CAPTURE (10–20 min) - additional items if node availability allows:
- journalctl -k --since "-24 hours" > kernel-journal-24h.log
- capture entire dmesg (compressed): dmesg > dmesg-raw-$(date -Iseconds).log && gzip it
- nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps --format=csv -l 500 (30s) to see in-flight clients
- nvlink counters: nvlink_sanity_dump.sh --all (script that gathers link counters per pair)
- driver stacktraces: echo 1 >/proc/sys/kernel/panic and use gdb /usr/libexec/driver-core to snapshot if driver is hung (ops only)
- /proc/interrupts and /proc/softirqs (to spot ballooning interrupts)
- collect hwmon readings for power/temps: for i in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do cat $i/temp*_input; done
- check BMC sensor dump: ipmitool sensor list > bmc-sensors.log
- nvlink firmware versions: read nvlink_firmver.txt via vendor utility
- run PCI bus rescan and capture response: echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan; capture dmesg delta

Naming convention for artifacts (important):
- incidentid_node_YYYYMMDDThhmmss_thing.log.gz
- example: SRE-7921-node-uint8-20280214T182312-dmesg.gz

Annotated quick heuristics (what to look for):
- Burst ECC then link flaps: if correctable ECC counters increment rapidly on one GPU immediately followed by nvlink retrain messages in kernel log, suspect link timing or cabling. Note pair of GPUs and which link index.
- Driver panic with backtrace: capture full stack and driver version. Check for known backtrace signatures in our tracker (see linked_artifacts). If matching old signature, escalate to serving-runtime team.
- BMC power events within 30s of kernel oops: treat as potential PSU/UPS/rails noise; collect BMC SEL and power rail sensor values.
- Persistent interrupts spike across GPUs: suggests IOMMU / PCIe root issues. Collect /proc/interrupts and consider temporary isolate-of-pci-slot for repro.

Sample dmesg excerpts to highlight (include lines in your FAST CAPTURE notes):
[ 1234.567890] GPU 0000:3b:00.0: corrected ECC error, 24 errors on DRAM
[ 1234.571112] nvlink: link 0x1b->0x1c: train_start timeout, retrying (attempt 3)
[ 1234.590010] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.592300] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[ 1234.593100] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000008

Capture artifact checklist to upload to incident (attach compressed):
- dmesg-raw-*.log.gz (required)
- kernel-journal-24h.log.gz (if available)
- nvlink-counters-YYYY.log (required if nvlink messages present)
- bmc-sensors.log (required if SEL contains events)
- nvidia-smi-snapshot.csv (required)
- notes.txt (always)

Triage decision matrix (first 20 minutes):
- If FAST CAPTURE shows repeated ECC->nvlink->driver sequence AND node is stable: quarantine node from traffic (set weight 0), open SRE-DRIVER ticket, attach artifacts, and schedule dedicated lab repro.
- If SEL/BMC shows power glitches within ±30s of kernel panic: treat as hardware noisy path: escalate to infra-hw for PSU/rack-level investigation.
- If dmesg shows single unique backtrace that matches an existing bug: trigger hotpatch/rollback plan; follow serving-runtime playbook for driver rollback.
- If no smoking gun and resets continue: enable increased telemetry sampling (see follow-up steps) and rotate node out of pool.

Follow-up steps (post-capture):
- Increase nvlink/driver debug level for 48h on suspect node (config: /etc/modprobe.d/nvlink-debug.conf) and collect ring buffer logs to long-term storage.
- Provision a lab node with identical firmware and attempt controlled repro with synthetic ECC load (small kernel that flips patterns). See reproducer repo link in linked_artifacts.
- If reproducer fails, schedule on-site cabling inspection and slotted swap of PCIe riser; correlate with ambient temp/power rails.

Common mistakes and anti-patterns:
- Rebooting immediately and losing ring buffer. Always do FAST CAPTURE pre-reboot if possible.
- Collecting only nvidia-smi snapshots without kernel logs. The sequence of kernel messages often contains the root cause.
- Renaming artifacts without incident id. Hard to map later.

Playbook snippets (commands to copy):
# FAST CAPTURE single command bundle
mkdir -p /tmp/incident-SRE-7921/$(date -Iseconds) && cd $_ || exit
journalctl -u kmod-driver -S "-1 hour" --no-pager > journal-driver.log &
dmesg | tail -n 200 > dmesg-tail.log &
( sleep 0.5; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv -lms 1000 -f nvidia-smi-fast.csv & ) &
ipmitool sel elist recent > ipmi-sel.log || true
( lspci -vvv -s $(lspci | grep -i nvidia | awk '{print $1}') > lspci-gpu.log ) || true
wait && tar czf SRE-7921-quickbundle-$(hostname)-$(date -Iseconds).tgz *

Incident tagging and handoff notes for oncall:
- Use slack channel #sre-gpu with prefix [SRE-7921] and attach quickbundle tgz.
- Ping serving-runtime oncall if stacktrace present and label with driver build id.
- When quarantining node, leave a small annotation in the host metadata explaining which artifacts are attached and where in cloud storage.

Appendix: reproducibility signals we care about (short list)
- Same GPU index across multiple events in last 72h
- Same nvlink pair or link index flapping
- Same backtrace symbol sequence in driver panic
- BMC power event within 30s

Notes to self / TODO (what to bake into automation)
- Create a single-sleep systemd unit that collects FAST CAPTURE automatically on first OOPS and uploads to incident bucket.
- Add a lightweight nvlink counter exporter to node-exporter so we can graph per-link noise.
- Add incident tagging template in Console to automatically attach node metadata to SRE tickets.

Authors: Ananya Rao (SRE), Riley Park (SRE), contributions from Diego Mendez (serving-runtime).
